Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for New Zealand's response, folks! The two umpires are out to the middle and the entire Sri Lankan team can be seen in a team-huddle near the ropes before they spread out to the field. The Kiwi opening pair of Rachin Ravindra and Tim Robinson walk out to the crease. It will be Chamindu Wickramasinghe to kick off the run chase with the new ball.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Well then, the Kiwis have a huge challenging task cut out for them with 219 to chase. It is not going to be an easy one for the hosts. Anything that had pace was smashed out of the park and the Lankans do have a bowling attack which is known for its pace variations as well. It is going to be a delicious run chase on the other side. Stay tuned.

The Kiwis remained under constant pressure as Kusal Perera's swashbuckling batting display powered him to his maiden T20I century. The hosts found no respite while Perera was at the crease. However, once two new batters came in, New Zealand managed to regain some control, restricting Sri Lanka to just 12 runs in the final two overs through some good death bowling by Duffy and Mitchell.

But it was in the mid-overs when Sri Lanka consolidated the start they got. The batters quickly cashed on anything that was served outside off with pace and also survived a couple of dropped catches to add to their misery. Kusal Perera reached his half-century during this period, where most overs yielded runs in excess and around 9 rpo. The acceleration was particularly evident between overs 10 and 16, as they amassed 84 runs in this crucial phase without losing a single wicket. Kusal Perera and Charith Asalanka constructed a centurion partnership on the back of some brilliant strokes played by the two southpaws.

In the early overs, the new ball offered considerable assistance to the pace bowlers through movement off the seam and swing. Santner made an immediate impact upon introducing himself into the attack, striking in his first over. He tried to stem the run flow by constant shuffling in the bowling. However, Kusal Perera showed positive intent from the outset, scoring freely. With the ball softening, Perera and Avishka began taking calculated risks against the spinners. Although the spin duo created several half-chances, the third-wicket stand continued to grow, only before Duffy was reintroduced and removed the latter.

A clinical batting performance by Sri Lanka, despite those last two quiet overs in the backend. But, with 218 on the board, the Lankans would be quite delighted as the batters have done their job sincerely. Despite conditions delaying the start due to a wet outfield, play eventually commenced beneath cloudy skies. The batting surface proved a bit challenging initially, with the New Zealand bowlers exploiting the conditions well in the first few overs. While Sri Lanka's opening pair of Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis managed to build a good foundation, their attempts to accelerate the scoring rate led to both wickets falling in quick succession.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! Well, it has been quite a balanced game so far. New Zealand has managed to get three wickets but the scoring rate has equally remained in excess or around 9 runs per over. The Sri Lanka top order did get some starts but they were prevented from building those into something substantial due to constant reshuffling in bowling changes by Santner. We are almost at the halfway stage of the first innings and the Sri Lankan middle order will now be under examination to prove itself. While New Zealand would like to get some more wickets quickly to exert more pressure on the tourists. Charith Asalanka walks out to the middle at number 5 for Sri Lanka.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND TAKEN! Mitchell Santner strikes in his very first over and a huge wicket for New Zealand as Kusal Mendis departs! Santner drops a flighted-delivery and lands it on off with a bit of a turn. It lands and just holds onto the surface for a bit and comes late on the bat. Kusal Mendis is early into his pull shot and tries to play it aerially. Goes through the shot, but mistimes it behind mid-wicket. Michael Bracewell at mid-wicket runs to his right, locks his eyes on the ball by backtracking it and takes a sharp catch while tumbling over. Sri Lanka lose their second wicket as Kusal Mendis 22 off 16.
Commentary.Howout: c Michael Bracewell b Mitchell Santner
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Mitchell Santner to Kusal Mendis, OUT! c Michael Bracewell b Mitchell Santner.

Zakary Foulkes bowls it from over the stumps and gets a huge inward curve which slides down leg, Kusal Mendis tries to pull the ball and swivels to go through the shot. Gets a faint edge off the blade and Mitchell Hay does extremely well to grab it low and left of him. FREE HIT TO FOLLOW NOW!

OUT! IN THE AIR AND TAKEN! New Zealand get their first breakthrough, but just for a brief moment, Mitchell Hay almost ran into the fence with the ball in hand. A well-directed short-pitched bumper from Henry, on the middle stump line. Pathum Nissanka swivels for another pull shot but plays a bit too close to the body. He does go through the shot and gets a thick top edge. It sails behind the keeper as Mitchell Hay tracks it backward. Locks his eyes on the ball and pouches it safely. He, however, keeps on running towards the fence with the momentum. As soon as he realises that he is about to cross the ropes, he lobs the ball up in the air, comes back into the field of play and grabs it safely. Nissanka departs and Sri Lanka are 30/1.
Commentary.Howout: c Mitchell Hay b Matt Henry
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Matt Henry to Pathum Nissanka, OUT! c Mitchell Hay b Matt Henry.

Commentary.Commentary: Well then, all in preparedness for the commencement of the third and final T20I. A sell-out crowd at the Saxton Oval, Nelson as well. Also, pleasing scenes as the sun is peeking out of the clouds. There's a fair share of thick cloud cover at one end, but, for the bare minimum, it is least threatening for the match to start now. The two umpires walk out to the middle, and the New Zealand players also scatter out to the field. Kusal Mendis and Pathum Nissanka are the two Sri Lankan openers who walk out to the crease. It will be Matt Henry to kick off the proceedings with the new ball. All players and the crowd are requested to observe a minute of silence as a tribute to the passing away of Senior Sergeant, Lyn Fleming with the personnel from the Nelson police force also present at the boundary side. Well then, all in readiness. Off we go...

PITCH REPORT - Katie Martin and Craig McMillan are inspecting the pitch at the Saxton Oval. Katie hopes that the rain will stay away and they will have all 40 overs bowled. Also mentions that there were a few concerns in the outfield and those have been cleared now. Informs that the boundary dimensions are slightly smaller than Mount Maunganui and says that it is 64 meters and 63 meters on either side. McMillan joins her and says that there's good grass coverage and it will aid pace and bounce.

New Zealand (Unchanged Playing XI) - Tim Robinson, Rachin Ravindra, Mark Chapman, Glenn Phillips, Daryl Mitchell, Mitchell Hay (WK), Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner (C), Zakary Foulkes, Matt Henry, Jacob Duffy.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Kusal Perera, Avishka Fernando, Charith Asalanka (C), Bhanuka Rajapaksa (In for Kamindu Mendis), Wanindu Hasaranga, Chamindu Wickramasinghe (In for Matheesha Pathirana), Maheesh Theekshana, Binura Fernando, Nuwan Thushara.

Charith Asalanka, the skipper of Sri Lanka says that the wicket looks the same as the previous two games. Mentions that they need to get their basics correct. Also believes that they weren't able to finish games and the middle order needs to capitalize and score runs quickly. Informs that they have two changes in the side, Bhanuka Rajapaksa and Chamindu Wickramasinghe come in the side. Also mentions that Matheesha Pathirana and Kamindu Mendis are out.

Mitchell Santner, the skipper of New Zealand says that due to overcast conditions, it is better to bowl first. Also says that the pitch has been under the covers for a bit and they want to see if they can make use of it. Adds that it is all about making guys comfortable in their roles. Appreciates the ground staff by saying they have done an excellent job. Informs that they are going unchanged and want to give young guys more opportunities.
TOSS UPDATE - The flip of the coin lands in favor of Mitchell Santner and New Zealand elects to BOWL first.

The two officiating umpires are now having a detailed discussion with the fourth umpire. We might have an official start time pretty soon. Let's hope for the best. Stay tuned.

UPDATE - 5.28 am IST (11.58 pm GMT, the previous day) - Not an official word, but according to the Blackcaps' social media posts, there might be an inspection by the umpires at 5.30 am IST (12 am GMT). It also mentions that the ground staff is working hard to prepare the ground following heavy overnight rain in Nelson. Stay tuned for further updates.

Well, it rained pretty heavily for a couple of days in Central New Zealand, but according to the latest reports, the rain Gods have been kind today. It is not raining as of now, but the outfield is still not favorable and ready enough for the play to commence. Hence, the toss has been OFFICIALLY DELAYED due to wet outfield!

The Saxton Oval, with its traditionally batting-friendly surface, could provide the perfect stage for a competitive finale to this T20I series. The relatively shorter boundaries might also encourage both teams to play more attacking cricket, setting up what promises to be an entertaining encounter. Stay tuned as the toss and the team updates are up next.

Sri Lanka's struggles in run chases have highlighted concerns about their batting tempo as they have lost both matches while chasing the target. A key issue has been the recent quiet form of promising youngster Kamindu Mendis, whose performance is crucial for strengthening their middle order. Meanwhile, New Zealand has benefited from Mitch Hay's stability in the lower middle order, though they're still waiting for Rachin Ravindra to find his rhythm at the top of the batting lineup.

Sri Lanka, meanwhile, are in a position where pride is at stake. Facing the prospect of a clean sweep on New Zealand soil, they'll be desperate to salvage something from this series before the format switches to ODIs. While the batters have displayed flashes of brilliance, especially Pathum Nissanka who leads the run-charts and is the only one to cross triple figures, by being the only of the batters to have made meaningful contributions. It is in the bowling department where the Lankans have found themselves in a bit of a pickle. The likes of Matheesha Pathirana have been really underwhelming with the spin department largely dependent on Maheesh Theekshana. The tourists will be aiming to put on a much more spirited performance to save their pride.

Under Mitchell Santner's astute leadership, this relatively inexperienced New Zealand side has shown remarkable composure and skill. After a somewhat tentative start in the series opener, the Blackcaps' top order has found its rhythm, with Daryl Mitchell particularly impressive in anchoring the middle order and providing crucial momentum in the death overs. The bowling unit has been equally impressive, with captain Santner leading by example in the spin department. Jacob Duffy has been a revelation with the ball, maintaining exceptional economy rates while consistently picking up wickets. His disciplined line and length have given the Sri Lankan batters precious little to work with.

As the cricket caravan rolls south from Mount Maunganui to Nelson's picturesque Saxton Oval, New Zealand find themselves in an enviable position with an unassailable 2-0 lead in the T20I series against Sri Lanka. On that note, we welcome you all to our coverage of this third and final T20I, before the action shifts to Wellington for the ODI leg of the tour. This also marks the first men's international match of 2025.
... MATCH DAY ...

The caravan now moves to Nelson for the third and final T20I of the series between New Zealand and Sri Lanka. With the series already decided, New Zealand head into this contest with an unassailable 2-0 lead, thanks to back-to-back wins in Mount Maunganui. In the second T20I, New Zealand posted a commanding total of 186, a target that proved insurmountable for Sri Lanka. The visitors faltered in their chase, collapsing dramatically to lose 7 wickets for just 14 runs and being bowled out for 141. While the top three, Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis, and Kusal Perera, have shown promise, the middle and lower order are yet to make meaningful contributions. Players like Charith Asalanka, Avishka Fernando, and Kamindu Mendis will be keen to find form and carry momentum into the ODI series. On the bowling front, Sri Lanka’s death bowling remains a significant concern with Wanindu Hasaranga being a shining light, delivering standout performances in both games. For New Zealand, Jacob Duffy has stood out, consistently delivering crucial breakthroughs whenever called upon. He has been well-supported by the rest of the attack. On the batting front, it was a collective effort from the Kiwis in the previous encounter. However, Rachin Ravindra has yet to hit his stride with the bat and will look to find form ahead of the ODI leg. With the series secured, New Zealand might take this opportunity to give game time to players who haven’t featured yet. As both Matt Henry and Jacob Duffy are part of the ODI squad, one of them could be rested to ensure they remain fresh and ready for the upcoming challenges. Will the Kiwis complete a dominant whitewash, or can Sri Lanka salvage some pride and finish the series on a high note? We shall find out.
